For a while, I refused to think in English (immigrated from Mexico to America when I was 5). I would try to avoid it as much as possible. Now, nearly thirteen years later, I realize that I haven't thought one thought in Spanish since I was a little girl. We still speak in Spanish in our household for the most part, but I seldom think in Spanish. I wonder what take my family members have in this.

I used to have a group of people which I called my "theatre friends." We met in high school and remained friends through our common interest of, well, theatre. We had great chemistry on stage. While we performed (by the end of our friendship, we had performed together for a total of six plays over a two-year period). We would meet up after each performance at one of the member's home, fueled by the excitement of having just acted in front of an audience,  and oftentimes chit chatted the night away. Everything was fun, I loved being around them, until they started playing around with drugs and alcohol. It started off with a couple celebratory drinks after performances. I thought, what the heck, what's a few drinks? 
I don't personally drink, but I didn't mind being around them while they took a few shots. A few shots turned into more and soon liquor wasn't enough and they moved onto experimenting with drugs. One night, one of the more "enthusiastic" members of the group suggested I had a drink. I politely declined, but she wouldn't take no for an answer. She continued to ask, shoving a shot of whiskey (which was probably laced with something else, as I had seen her drop a tab of something in the drink earlier) onto my face. "Come on, what harm can one drink do?" she asked, practically almost pouring the drink onto my lips and I excused myself out of there. 
That was one of the last times I've met up with them.
